clipd — session clipboard

clipd --session vt1|vt3|vt4 owns the clipboard service on that graphical session's broker, under the name clipd. It connects using WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, prefers ext-data-control-v1 and uses wlr data control v2 only when ext is absent. --seat NAME overrides the first non-agent seat. It watches both clipboard and PRIMARY without requiring keyboard focus.

Commands and events

CommandBody and result
clipboard.get{mime?, primary?, offset?} → {mime,data,encoding,size,offset,next_offset,eof,sensitive,stamp}
clipboard.set{mime,data,encoding?,primary?,sensitive?,stamp?}; encoding is utf8 (default) or base64, at most 1 MiB decoded
clipboard.clear{primary?}; clears the selected clipboard
clipboard.history{} → up to 50 text entries, newest first
clipboard.pick{n}; sets the zero-based history entry
clipboard.info{} → session, protocol, caps and configured peers
clipboard.push{to:"vt4"}; the equivalent desk-prefixed alias is also accepted
desktop.clipboard.menuOpens Klipper on Plasma, or the native history picker in a desk
desktop.clipboard.rotateChooses the next history entry

clipboard.changed publishes {session,generation,origin_session,mime_types, size,sensitive,primary}. It contains metadata only. Size is null when unknown; for text it is the cached text size. stamp is {origin_session,generation}; generations are UUIDs and are never reused after a daemon restart. Replayed sets are ignored within the bounded loop guard. A Wayland marker identifies the service's own selection echoes.

clipboard.get returns at most 1 MiB per call; continue with next_offset until eof. UTF-8 slices use encoding:"utf8"; arbitrary bytes, including a slice that cuts a multibyte character, use encoding:"base64". Materialisation is capped at 64 MiB with a five-second Wayland read deadline.

History is in memory and holds only valid UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB per entry. x-kde-passwordManagerHint with value secret, unreadable hints and explicit sensitive:true sets never enter history or cross sessions. Content commands admit only broker-stamped local-session callers.

Mix provides clip_get([mime]) (a UTF-8 string or binary bytes, at most 1 MiB) and clip_set(text[, mime]). Binary decoding uses Mix's crypto feature, included in the native shell. They use the local broker's clipd; failures raise. The MCP tools are clipboard_get and clipboard_set and likewise target the local session. Use the Bus commands for binary or chunked reads.

Same-host push

Cross-session sharing is off by default. --settings FILE reads a schema-1 strict-data .conf.mix document. Provision one private random 32-byte file for one logical user on one host, exposing a private copy to that user's mapped account in each isolated desk. Each copy must be owned by its session user with no group/other permissions. Do not distribute it to mesh nodes on other hosts. This credential is the scope authority; hostnames and numeric UID claims on the wire confer no authority.

{
  schema: 1,
  scope_key_file: "/home/user/.config/mixos/clipboard.scope",
  eager_text_bytes: 1048576,
  peers: {
    vt4: {target:"clipd.alpha.example.bus", images:false, follow:false}
  }
}

Configure the reciprocal peer on the other session. Targets are exact native Bus routes; only vt1, vt3 and vt4 are admitted. Other nodes cannot receive or fetch a transfer without this host/user credential. Transfer requests and replies use authenticated encryption over the existing Bus, bind destination and command, expire after 30 seconds and reject replayed nonces.

Cached small text travels eagerly, capped at 1 MiB total by default. The target advertises the complete original list; uncached MIME types, larger text and images use 64 KiB Bus chunks only when a client requests that MIME. Both ends must allow images:true for images. The original source generation must still exist until that type is materialised; the target can then serve its bounded cache. A replaced selection, missing service, timeout or cap failure closes the paste fd cleanly and logs the failure. Forwarded lazy offers retain their origin stamp; fetches carry a bounded session path and fail cleanly if a dependency cycle is detected. Optional follow:true pushes local changes to that peer; imported changes do not trigger follow. Nothing follows by default.

clipboard.receive and clipboard.fetch are internal encrypted peer commands. Ordinary mesh calls to content commands are refused; explicit push is the supported cross-session path.

Units and keys

The component ships units/clipd.service for the host's systemd user manager and units/clipd@.service for desk sessions, using the same environment file as the compositor. Shared desks override User= like the other desk units. The host user manager must inherit the graphical session's Wayland variables. Use a service drop-in to add --settings for sharing. Units are templates for mix layout apply; shipping them does not install or enable them.

inputd migrates the existing Right Ctrl+Down/Up clipboard rows from the old desktop-vt1 target to clipd, retaining their menu/rotate actions. Custom targets and unrelated user bindings are preserved. Plasma keeps Klipper's history UI through its existing session API; desks use the native picker. clipd does not take ownership just to observe a selection.
